subject: Request: limited-term parity pilot & procurement timeline
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@brightline.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intro: displacement pilot inquiry

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking a call last week. Brightline is evaluating options to displace our current OpenAI + managed endpoint stack for production chat and assistant features. Procurement asked me to get an explicit parity + short-term pilot offer from your team to evaluate unit economics and latency in our environment.

Key asks from our side:
- Per-token parity to current spend for a 90-day pilot (we're currently paying $0.0008/1k tokens net on our committed OpenAI plan; looking for comparable effective rate)
- Commitment tier for pilot: 30M–75M tokens/month (we can scale inside that window)
- SLA targets (p95 latency & availability) and rollback/fallback plan if quality drops
- Standard SOC2 evidence and a working procurement timeline (we need PO or contract by end of month)

I've attached the RFP Q&A (Brightline_RFP_QA.pdf) with our traffic profile and sample prompts. Mike Harris (cc) will drive procurement logistics.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can do a limited-term parity pilot and what the commercial terms would look like?

Best,
Sara Patel
Head of Product Partnerships
Brightline AI

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@brightline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intro: displacement pilot inquiry

Sara —

Appreciate the clear asks and the traffic snapshot. Short answer: yes, we can run a constrained parity pilot, but we need clarity on a couple of items to structure it safely for both parties. Attached is a one-page parity term sheet (parity_term_sheet_v1.pdf) that outlines how we’d operationalize a 90-day pilot and the fallback protections. High-level proposal:

- Pilot duration: 90 days; Brightline commits to minimum 30M tokens/month during the pilot window.
- Pricing: effective per-token rate matched to your current net rate for the pilot window (we'll require a short-term usage commitment and an initial prepayment/credit to offset spin-up costs).
- Credit mechanics: pilot credits are applied to future committed capacity if Brightline converts to a Reserved plan within 120 days. Otherwise credits are retained by Redwood.
- SLA: p95 latency target 220ms for the baseline workload in your profiles; 99.5% availability with automated fallback to our hosted standard model (slightly higher latency).
- Quality guardrail: we run a side-by-side eval on a seed prompt set; if the regression exceeds agreed thresholds, we pause parity pricing and execute a rollback plan.

Action items for both sides:
- From Brightline: finalize pilot monthly volume band (30/50/75M), provide final PO contact and SOC2 contact.
- From Redwood: provide parity term sheet, SOC2 evidence pack, and a draft contract + minimal SOW for the pilot.

Ben — can you review the pricing rows in the attached term sheet and flag anything we shouldn’t expose at this stage? Lauren — please add the procurement checklist to the contract draft once Ben confirms.

Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to walk through.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Revenue
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Sara Patel <sara@brightline.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 08:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intro: displacement pilot inquiry

Sara / team — quick commercial note from my side. If Brightline wants parity on a short pilot while protecting Redwood economics, here's a pragmatic structure we use:

- Pilot bracket pricing (90 days): 30M @ $0.0009/token, 50M @ $0.00082/token, 75M @ $0.00075/token — all per-token prices are 'effective' after applying pilot credit.
- Prepayment: 50% of estimated pilot spend up-front (refundable vs. performance guardrail; becomes a credit on conversion).
- Conversion incentive: If Brightline converts to a reserved commit within 120 days, we apply all pilot prepayment as a dollar credit and move to a multi-tiered slab with blended lower rates.
- Procurement-friendly clause: We can provide a short Addendum with acceptance criteria and a 10-business-day termination for convenience during pilot (limited exposure).

Two quick operational asks: SOC2 Type II evidence (we'll push the pack), and clarifying what model families you want run under parity — more expensive models (larger-replica) will require a marginal uplift.

Lauren — can you confirm the minimal legal language for the procurement addendum and I'll coordinate the numbers with accounting.

Ben Carter
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Feb 16, 2027 at 08:05 AM PST Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sara —
>
> Appreciate the clear asks and the traffic snapshot. Short answer: yes, we can run a constrained parity pilot...

From: Sara Patel <sara@brightline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Harris <mike.harris@brightline.ai>, procurement@brightline.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intro: displacement pilot inquiry

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what procurement needs. We'd like to move forward with the 50M bracket at your $0.00082/token effective rate, pending:

1) SOC2 pack and the parity term sheet you attached
2) A short SOW + addendum that includes the 10-business-day convenience termination during the pilot (procurement insisted)
3) DocuSign-ready contract by Feb 24 so we can route for PO and finance approvals

I'll attach our procurement timeline (Brightline_procurement_timeline.xlsx) and loop in procurement contact. Once you send the DocuSign link we'll get signatures and fund the prepayment.

DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/brightline-parity-draft
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deals/BR-2048

Looking forward —
Sara
Head of Product Partnerships
Brightline AI
